records.source: וַיְהִ֕י כִּשְׁמֹ֖עַ יָבִ֣ין מֶֽלֶךְ־חָצ֑וֹר וַיִּשְׁלַ֗ח אֶל־יוֹבָב֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ מָד֔וֹן וְאֶל־מֶ֥לֶךְ שִׁמְר֖וֹן וְאֶל־מֶ֥לֶךְ אַכְשָֽׁף׃
records.gloss: And it was, when heard Jabin king of Hazor, and he sent to Jobab king of Madon and to [the] king of Shimron and to [the] king of Achshaph,
pieces: When Jabin king of Hazor heard of this, he sent word to Jobab king of Madon, to the king of Shimron, to the king of Achshaph,

L.1: And it came about, when Jabin king of Hazor heard [of it], that he sent to Jobab king of Madon, and to the king of Shimron, and to the king of Achshaph,

R.1: Jabin, the king of Hazor, heard what Israel had done. So he sent messages to Jobab, the king of Madon, and to the kings of Shimron and Achshaph.

decisions.choice: when Jabin heard: news of Israel's victories reaches the north
decisions.reason: The verse does not say what Jabin heard. The same opening begins the southern alliance in 10:1 and the gathering of kings in 9:1, and in each case the news is what Israel had done. Here it follows the victories in the south told in chapter 10.

decisions.choice: Jabin king of Hazor: the ruler of the leading city of the north
decisions.reason: Hazor lay north of the Sea of Galilee and was the largest city of the region; verse 10 calls it "the head of all these kingdoms", which is why its king calls the others together. A later king of Hazor named Jabin appears in Judges 4:2, so the name may have been used by more than one ruler of the city.

decisions.choice: Madon, Shimron, Achshaph: towns of the northern region
decisions.reason: These were towns of Galilee and the plain to its west. Shimron and Achshaph are named again in the borders of Zebulun and Asher (19:15, 25), and all three kings are in the list of 12:19-20. The exact sites are not certain.

decisions.choice: heard what Israel had done
decisions.reason: Readable says what Jabin heard, from the context (m1), and ends the sentence here; verses 2-3 each begin a new sentence instead of continuing the list.

records.heading: The kings of the north

records.source: וְֽאֶל־הַמְּלָכִ֞ים אֲשֶׁ֣ר מִצְּפ֗וֹן בָּהָ֧ר וּבָעֲרָבָ֛ה נֶ֥גֶב כִּֽנֲר֖וֹת וּבַשְּׁפֵלָ֑ה וּבְנָפ֥וֹת דּ֖וֹר מִיָּֽם׃
records.gloss: and to the kings who [were] from [the] north in the hill country, and in the Arabah south of Chinneroth, and in the Shephelah, and in heights of Dor from [the] west,
pieces: and to the kings of the north, those in the hill country, in the Arabah south of Chinneroth, in the foothills, and in the heights of Dor to the west,

L.2: and to the kings who [were] in the north, in the hill country and in the Arabah south of Chinneroth and in the Shephelah and in the heights of Dor on the west,

R.2: He also sent messages to the kings in the north. Some ruled in the hills, some in the Jordan Valley south of Lake Galilee, some in the low hills in the west, and some in the hills around Dor near the sea.

decisions.choice: the hill country, the Arabah, the Shephelah: the regions of the north
decisions.reason: The list names regions as in Deuteronomy 1:7: the hill country of Galilee; the Arabah, the Jordan valley; and the Shephelah, the low hills between the high ground and the coastal plain. Here they are the northern parts of each region.

decisions.choice: Chinneroth: the Sea of Galilee and the land beside it
decisions.reason: The lake later called the Sea of Galilee bears this name in Numbers 34:11 and Joshua 12:3 and 13:27. "South of Chinneroth" places these kings in the Jordan valley below the lake.

decisions.choice: the heights of Dor: the hilly ground near the coastal town of Dor
alternatives: Naphoth-dor, read as a place name
decisions.reason: The first word is uncommon and seems to mean heights or slopes. The same phrase appears as a district in 12:23 and 1 Kings 4:11. Dor was a town on the Mediterranean coast south of Mount Carmel, so "on the west" fits it.

decisions.choice: foothills (B); the Jordan Valley, the low hills in the west, Lake Galilee (R)
decisions.reason: As in Deuteronomy 1:7, Literal keeps the names Arabah and Shephelah, Balanced says "foothills" for the Shephelah, and Readable describes the regions. Readable also names the lake by its familiar name.

records.source: הַֽכְּנַעֲנִי֙ מִמִּזְרָ֣ח וּמִיָּ֔ם וְהָאֱמֹרִ֧י וְהַחִתִּ֛י וְהַפְּרִזִּ֥י וְהַיְבוּסִ֖י בָּהָ֑ר וְהַֽחִוִּי֙ תַּ֣חַת חֶרְמ֔וֹן בְּאֶ֖רֶץ הַמִּצְפָּֽה׃
records.gloss: the Canaanite[s] from [the] east and from [the] west, and the Amorite[s] and the Hittite[s] and the Perizzite[s] and the Jebusite[s] in the hill country, and the Hivite[s] under Hermon in [the] land of the Mizpah.
pieces: to the Canaanites in the east and the west, to the Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites and Jebusites in the hill country, and to the Hivites below Mount Hermon in the region of Mizpah.

L.3: [to] the Canaanites in the east and in the west, and the Amorites and the Hittites and the Perizzites and the Jebusites in the hill country, and the Hivites below Hermon in the land of Mizpah.

R.3: He sent to the Canaanites in the east and in the west. He sent to the Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites and Jebusites in the hills. And he sent to the Hivites who lived at the foot of Mount Hermon in the area of Mizpah.

decisions.choice: the Canaanite, the Amorite ...: each singular name stands for a whole people
decisions.reason: Hebrew often names a people with a singular form and the article, "the Canaanite", meaning all who belong to it (as in 3:10; 9:1). The list is the usual list of the peoples of the land, here placed in the north.

decisions.choice: Hermon; the land of Mizpah: the far north, at the foot of the great mountain
decisions.reason: Mount Hermon is the high mountain at the northern edge of the land (12:1; Deuteronomy 3:8-9). The name Mizpah, which has the article here, means "lookout" and was given to several places; this one is in the north, not the Mizpah of Benjamin (18:26). The "valley of Mizpeh" in verse 8 is probably the same area.

decisions.choice: [to] the Canaanites (L); to the Canaanites (B)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew continues the list of verse 2 without repeating "to". Literal brackets it; Balanced repeats it so the list stays clear. Balanced also adds "Mount" to Hermon.

decisions.choice: He sent to ... He sent to ... And he sent to ...
decisions.reason: Readable turns the long list into three short sentences, repeating the verb from verse 1.

records.source: וַיֵּצְא֣וּ הֵ֗ם וְכָל־מַֽחֲנֵיהֶם֙ עִמָּ֔ם עַם־רָ֕ב כַּח֛וֹל אֲשֶׁ֥ר עַל־שְׂפַת־הַיָּ֖ם לָרֹ֑ב וְס֥וּס וָרֶ֖כֶב רַב־מְאֹֽד׃
records.gloss: And they came out, they and all their camps with them, a people numerous like the sand that [is] on [the] shore of the sea for multitude, and horse[s] and chariot[s] many very.
pieces: They came out with all their forces, an army as countless as the sand along the seashore, with a great many horses and chariots.

L.4: And they came out, they and all their armies with them, a people as numerous as the sand that [is] on the shore of the sea in multitude, and very many horses and chariots.

R.4: These kings came out with all their armies. There were so many soldiers that no one could count them, like the grains of sand on the beach. They also had a huge number of horses and chariots.

decisions.choice: camps: armies in the field
decisions.reason: The word means a camp, and from that the army that camps in it (8:13; 10:5). Each king brought out his own troops.

decisions.choice: like the sand on the seashore: too many to count
decisions.reason: The picture is used for a number beyond counting, as in God's promise to Abraham (Genesis 22:17) and of the armies in Judges 7:12 and 1 Samuel 13:5. It describes how great the army was, not an exact size.

decisions.choice: horses and chariots: the strongest weapon of the time, which Israel did not have
decisions.reason: Chariots drawn by horses gave the Canaanite armies speed and force on open ground, and Israel's foot soldiers had nothing like them (17:16-18; Judges 1:19). Deuteronomy 20:1 had told Israel not to fear an army with horses and chariots greater than its own.

decisions.choice: an army
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "a people". Used of men who go out to fight, the word means a fighting force (8:1, 3), so Balanced says "army".

decisions.choice: so many soldiers that no one could count them
decisions.reason: Readable spells out what the comparison with sand means (m2) and then keeps the picture.

records.source: וַיִּוָּ֣עֲד֔וּ כֹּ֖ל הַמְּלָכִ֣ים הָאֵ֑לֶּה וַיָּבֹ֜אוּ וַיַּחֲנ֤וּ יַחְדָּו֙ אֶל־מֵ֣י מֵר֔וֹם לְהִלָּחֵ֖ם עִם־יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃פ
records.gloss: And met together all the kings these, and they came and camped together at [the] waters of Merom to fight with Israel.
pieces: All these kings joined forces; they came and camped together at the waters of Merom to fight against Israel.

L.5: And all these kings met together, and they came and camped together at the waters of Merom to fight with Israel.

R.5: All these kings agreed to meet and fight together. They came and set up camp by the waters of Merom to go to war against Israel.

decisions.choice: met together: gathered at an agreed time and place
decisions.reason: The verb is used of people who meet by appointment (Numbers 10:3-4; 14:35). The kings did not meet by chance; they made a plan together.

decisions.choice: the waters of Merom: springs or a stream in upper Galilee
decisions.reason: The place is named only here and in verse 7. It was near a town called Merom in the hills of upper Galilee, but the exact site is not known. The hilly ground there may have been chosen by the kings or forced on them; the text does not say.

decisions.choice: fight against Israel
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "fight with Israel", which means to fight against them. Balanced and Readable say "against" so it is not read as "on Israel's side".

records.source: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֣ה אֶל־יְהוֹשֻׁעַ֮ אַל־תִּירָ֣א מִפְּנֵיהֶם֒ כִּֽי־מָחָ֞ר כָּעֵ֣ת הַזֹּ֗את אָנֹכִ֞י נֹתֵ֧ן אֶת־כֻּלָּ֛ם חֲלָלִ֖ים לִפְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל אֶת־סוּסֵיהֶ֣ם תְּעַקֵּ֔ר וְאֶת־מַרְכְּבֹתֵיהֶ֖ם תִּשְׂרֹ֥ף בָּאֵֽשׁ׃
records.gloss: And said Yahweh to Joshua, not be afraid because of them, for tomorrow about the time this I [am] giving all of them slain before Israel; their horses you shall hamstring, and their chariots you shall burn with fire.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to Joshua, "Have no fear of them. At this hour tomorrow I will lay every one of them dead before Israel. You are to hamstring their horses and set fire to their chariots."

L.6: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Joshua, "Do not be afraid because of them, for tomorrow about this time I [am] giving all of them [over] slain before Israel. Their horses you shall hamstring, and their chariots you shall burn with fire."

R.6: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to Joshua, "Do not be afraid of them. By this time tomorrow I will have handed them all over to Israel, and they will lie dead. Cut the leg tendons of their horses so that they can never be used in war again, and burn their chariots."

decisions.choice: do not be afraid: the LORD's word of courage before battle
decisions.reason: The same words came to Joshua before the battles at Ai and Gibeon (8:1; 10:8), and they echo the LORD's charge in 1:9. Here they answer the size of the army in verse 4.

decisions.choice: I am giving them slain: a certain act in the near future
decisions.reason: The verb form describes what is about to happen as already under way. God himself is the one who gives the enemy over; "slain" says what they will be when he has done so.

decisions.choice: hamstring: cut the tendons at the back of the legs
decisions.reason: Cutting this tendon lames a horse so that it can no longer pull a chariot or be used in war. David did the same to the chariot horses he captured (2 Samuel 8:4).

decisions.choice: lame the horses and burn the chariots: Israel is not to keep them
decisions.reason: The verse gives no reason for the command. It means that Israel would not build up a chariot force of its own from the spoil. Elsewhere Israel's king is told not to multiply horses (Deuteronomy 17:16), and the people are told that victory comes from the LORD, not from horses and chariots (Deuteronomy 20:1; Psalm 20:8).

decisions.choice: I will lay every one of them dead before Israel
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps both the giving and "slain" in one clause. It also says "set fire to" for "burn with fire", the Hebrew's fuller way of saying "burn".

decisions.choice: Cut the leg tendons of their horses so that they can never be used in war again
decisions.reason: "Hamstring" is not a word most young readers know, so Readable says what was done and why it mattered (m3).

records.heading: Victory over the northern kings

records.source: וַיָּבֹ֣א יְהוֹשֻׁ֡עַ וְכָל־עַם֩ הַמִּלְחָמָ֨ה עִמּ֧וֹ עֲלֵיהֶ֛ם עַל־מֵ֥י מֵר֖וֹם פִּתְאֹ֑ם וַֽיִּפְּל֖וּ בָּהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And came Joshua and all [the] people of the war with him against them at [the] waters of Merom suddenly, and they fell on them.
pieces: So Joshua and all his fighting men came upon them suddenly at the waters of Merom and attacked them.

L.7: And Joshua and all the people of war with him came against them at the waters of Merom suddenly, and they fell on them.

R.7: So Joshua and all his soldiers made a surprise attack on the kings' armies at the waters of Merom.

decisions.choice: the people of war: the fighting men
decisions.reason: The phrase names the men fit for battle, as in 8:1, 3 and 10:7.

decisions.choice: suddenly: without warning
decisions.reason: Joshua strikes before the kings expect him, as he did at Gibeon after a night march (10:9).

decisions.choice: fell on them: attacked them
decisions.reason: To "fall on" an enemy is to attack it (Judges 8:21; 1 Samuel 22:17-18).

decisions.choice: the kings' armies
decisions.reason: Readable names who "them" are, from verses 4-5, and joins "suddenly" and "fell on them" as "a surprise attack".

records.source: וַיִּתְּנֵ֨ם יְהוָ֥ה בְּיַֽד־יִשְׂרָאֵל֮ וַיַּכּוּם֒ וַֽיִּרְדְּפ֞וּם עַד־צִיד֣וֹן רַבָּ֗ה וְעַד֙ מִשְׂרְפ֣וֹת מַ֔יִם וְעַד־בִּקְעַ֥ת מִצְפֶּ֖ה מִזְרָ֑חָה וַיַּכֻּ֕ם עַד־בִּלְתִּ֥י הִשְׁאִֽיר־לָהֶ֖ם שָׂרִֽיד׃
records.gloss: And gave them Yahweh into [the] hand of Israel, and they struck them and pursued them as far as Sidon great and as far as Misrephoth-maim and as far as [the] valley of Mizpeh eastward; and they struck them until not was left to them a survivor.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} handed them over to Israel, who defeated them and chased them to Great Sidon and Misrephoth-maim, and toward the east to the valley of Mizpeh. They kept striking them down until not one was left.

L.8: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave them into the hand of Israel, and they struck them and pursued them as far as Great Sidon, and as far as Misrephoth-maim, and as far as the valley of Mizpeh to the east; and they struck them until no survivor was left to them.

R.8: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} gave Israel the victory over them. The Israelites beat them and chased them all the way to the great city of Sidon and to Misrephoth-maim. They also chased them east as far as the valley of Mizpeh. They kept fighting until no one was left alive.

decisions.choice: gave them into the hand of Israel: gave Israel victory over them
decisions.reason: "Into the hand" means into someone's power. The victory is said first to be the LORD's doing, as he promised in verse 6.

decisions.choice: Great Sidon, Misrephoth-maim, the valley of Mizpeh: the routes of the flight, north-west and east
decisions.reason: Sidon was the chief city of the Phoenician coast, far to the north-west; "Great Sidon" may mean the city with its lands (19:28). Misrephoth-maim was near the coast on the way there (13:6), though its site is not certain. The valley of Mizpeh lay to the east, below Hermon (verse 3). The beaten army fled in more than one direction, and Israel followed each group.

decisions.choice: until no survivor was left: the army was completely broken
decisions.reason: The phrase is used in Joshua for a complete victory (8:22; 10:28, 33). It describes the end of the fleeing army as a fighting force.

decisions.choice: toward the east to the valley of Mizpeh (B); They also chased them east (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced puts "toward the east" first to show that this was a second line of pursuit, away from the coast. Readable makes it a sentence of its own.

records.source: וַיַּ֤עַשׂ לָהֶם֙ יְהוֹשֻׁ֔עַ כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר אָֽמַר־ל֖וֹ יְהוָ֑ה אֶת־סוּסֵיהֶ֣ם עִקֵּ֔ר וְאֶת־מַרְכְּבֹתֵיהֶ֖ם שָׂרַ֥ף בָּאֵֽשׁ׃ס
records.gloss: And did to them Joshua just as had said to him Yahweh: their horses he hamstrung, and their chariots he burned with fire.
pieces: Joshua did to them just as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had told him: he hamstrung their horses and set fire to their chariots.

L.9: And Joshua did to them as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had said to him: their horses he hamstrung, and their chariots he burned with fire.

R.9: Joshua did to them what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had told him to do. He crippled their horses so that they could not be used in war, and he burned their chariots.

decisions.choice: just as the LORD had said: the command of verse 6 carried out
decisions.reason: The verse repeats the words of verse 6 almost exactly, now in the past, to show that Joshua obeyed in every detail. On the meaning of the command, see verse 6.

decisions.choice: crippled their horses so that they could not be used in war
decisions.reason: As in verse 6, Readable explains "hamstring" in plain words.

records.source: וַיָּ֨שָׁב יְהוֹשֻׁ֜עַ בָּעֵ֤ת הַהִיא֙ וַיִּלְכֹּ֣ד אֶת־חָצ֔וֹר וְאֶת־מַלְכָּ֖הּ הִכָּ֣ה בֶחָ֑רֶב כִּֽי־חָצ֣וֹר לְפָנִ֔ים הִ֕יא רֹ֖אשׁ כָּל־הַמַּמְלָכ֥וֹת הָאֵֽלֶּה׃
records.gloss: And turned back Joshua at the time that and captured Hazor, and its king he struck with the sword; for Hazor formerly, it [was the] head of all the kingdoms these.
pieces: At that time Joshua came back and took Hazor; he put its king to the sword, for Hazor had once been the leading power among all these kingdoms.

L.10: And Joshua turned back at that time and captured Hazor, and its king he struck with the sword; for Hazor formerly [was] the head of all these kingdoms.

R.10: Then Joshua turned back and captured the city of Hazor. He killed its king with the sword. In those days Hazor had been the most powerful of all these kingdoms.

decisions.choice: turned back: returned from the pursuit
decisions.reason: After chasing the beaten armies far to the north-west and east (verse 8), Joshua comes back to deal with the city that led the alliance.

decisions.choice: the head of all these kingdoms: the chief city, the leader of the alliance
decisions.reason: "Head" means the first or ruling one. This is why the call to war came from Jabin king of Hazor (verse 1).

decisions.choice: formerly: before its fall, from the writer's later point of view
decisions.reason: The word looks back from the time of writing to what Hazor had been. The same way of speaking appears in 14:15 and 15:15, where towns are given their former names.

decisions.choice: put its king to the sword
decisions.reason: Balanced uses a natural English phrase for "struck with the sword", meaning killed in battle or executed.

records.heading: Hazor is burned

records.source: וַ֠יַּכּוּ אֶת־כָּל־הַנֶּ֨פֶשׁ אֲשֶׁר־בָּ֤הּ לְפִי־חֶ֨רֶב֙ הַֽחֲרֵ֔ם לֹ֥א נוֹתַ֖ר כָּל־נְשָׁמָ֑ה וְאֶת־חָצ֖וֹר שָׂרַ֥ף בָּאֵֽשׁ׃
records.gloss: And they struck every person who [was] in it with [the] mouth of [the] sword, devoting to destruction; not was left any breath, and Hazor he burned with fire.
pieces: They put everyone in it to the sword, devoting them to destruction, and no one who breathed was left. Then Joshua burned Hazor.

L.11: And they struck every person who [was] in it with the edge of the sword, devoting [them] to destruction; there was not left any [one] that breathed. And he burned Hazor with fire.

R.11: They killed everyone in the city with their swords. They destroyed them completely, as people given over to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. No one was left alive. Then Joshua set fire to Hazor.

decisions.choice: the mouth of the sword: the edge of the sword
decisions.reason: Hebrew speaks of a sword's "mouth", the edge that "eats" (2 Samuel 2:26). To strike with it is to kill in battle.

decisions.choice: devoting to destruction: giving the people over wholly to the LORD by destroying them
decisions.reason: This is the verb of the "devoted thing" (Leviticus 27:28-29). In war it means that the enemy is destroyed and nothing is kept for gain (Deuteronomy 7:2; 20:16-17; Joshua 6:17-21). On the hard questions this command raises, see the note at Deuteronomy 7:2 and verse 20 below.

decisions.choice: any breath: any living person
decisions.reason: The word means breath, and so a living being. As in Deuteronomy 20:16 it refers to people here: verse 14 shows that the livestock were kept.

decisions.choice: destroyed them completely, as people given over to the LORD
decisions.reason: As in Deuteronomy 7:2, Readable gives the sense of the term in plain words; Literal and Balanced keep "devote to destruction".

decisions.choice: Joshua
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "he burned"; verse 13 shows that "he" is Joshua. Balanced and Readable name him.

records.source: וְֽאֶת־כָּל־עָרֵ֣י הַמְּלָכִֽים־הָ֠אֵלֶּה וְֽאֶת־כָּל־מַלְכֵיהֶ֞ם לָכַ֧ד יְהוֹשֻׁ֛עַ וַיַּכֵּ֥ם לְפִי־חֶ֖רֶב הֶחֱרִ֣ים אוֹתָ֑ם כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר צִוָּ֔ה מֹשֶׁ֖ה עֶ֥בֶד יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: And all [the] cities of the kings these and all their kings captured Joshua, and he struck them with [the] mouth of [the] sword; he devoted them to destruction, just as had commanded Moses [the] servant of Yahweh.
pieces: Joshua captured all the towns of these kings, and their kings as well, and put them to the sword. He devoted them to destruction, just as Moses the servant of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded.

L.12: And all the cities of these kings, and all their kings, Joshua captured, and he struck them with the edge of the sword; he devoted them to destruction, as Moses the slave of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded.

R.12: Joshua captured all the towns of these kings, and he captured the kings too. He killed them with the sword. He destroyed them completely, as people given over to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. This is what Moses, the servant of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, had commanded.

decisions.choice: as Moses had commanded: the command of Deuteronomy carried out
decisions.reason: Moses had commanded that the peoples of the land be devoted to destruction (Deuteronomy 7:1-2; 20:16-17). Verses 12, 15 and 20 each tie what Joshua did to that command.

decisions.choice: the servant of the LORD: Moses' title of honor
decisions.reason: As in 1:1: the word is the word for a slave, one who belongs wholly to his master, and said of Moses and God it is a title of honor.

decisions.choice: slave (L); servant (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in 1:1, Literal keeps the hard sense of the word, and Balanced and Readable say "servant".

decisions.choice: towns
decisions.reason: As in Deuteronomy 2:34: "cities" at Literal, "towns" at Balanced and Readable, since most were small walled places.

records.source: רַ֣ק כָּל־הֶעָרִ֗ים הָעֹֽמְדוֹת֙ עַל־תִּלָּ֔ם לֹ֥א שְׂרָפָ֖ם יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל זוּלָתִ֛י אֶת־חָצ֥וֹר לְבַדָּ֖הּ שָׂרַ֥ף יְהוֹשֻֽׁעַ׃
records.gloss: Only all the cities standing on their mounds, not burned them Israel, except Hazor alone; [it] burned Joshua.
pieces: But Israel did not burn any of the towns that stood on their mounds, except Hazor alone, which Joshua burned.

L.13: Only, all the cities that stood on their mounds, Israel did not burn them, except Hazor alone; Joshua burned [it].

R.13: But the Israelites did not burn the other towns that were built on mounds. Hazor was the only one Joshua burned.

decisions.choice: stood on their mounds: towns built on the raised mounds of earlier towns
alternatives: the towns that were still standing intact
decisions.reason: A town in that land was often rebuilt again and again on the ruins of the one before, until it stood on a hill of its own making. The word for such a mound is used in Deuteronomy 13:17 and Jeremiah 30:18. The phrase may also mean that the towns were left standing where they were, whole.

decisions.choice: only ... except Hazor alone: Hazor's burning was the exception
decisions.reason: Most towns were taken and left to be lived in, as Deuteronomy 6:10-11 had promised: towns Israel had not built (Joshua 24:13). Only Hazor, the head of the alliance, was burned.

decisions.choice: all the cities ..., Israel did not burn them
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew order, which puts the cities first and picks them up again with "them".

decisions.choice: the other towns
decisions.reason: Readable says "other" to make plain that Hazor is set apart from the rest.

records.source: וְ֠כֹל שְׁלַ֞ל הֶעָרִ֤ים הָאֵ֨לֶּה֙ וְהַבְּהֵמָ֔ה בָּזְז֥וּ לָהֶ֖ם בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל רַ֣ק אֶֽת־כָּל־הָאָדָ֞ם הִכּ֣וּ לְפִי־חֶ֗רֶב עַד־הִשְׁמִדָם֙ אוֹתָ֔ם לֹ֥א הִשְׁאִ֖ירוּ כָּל־נְשָׁמָֽה׃
records.gloss: And all [the] spoil of the cities these and the livestock plundered for themselves [the] sons of Israel; only every human they struck with [the] mouth of [the] sword until they had destroyed them; not they left any breath.
pieces: The {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} took all the spoil of these towns and the livestock for themselves. But every human being they killed with the sword until they had wiped them out; they left no one alive.

L.14: And all the spoil of these cities and the livestock the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel plundered for themselves; only every human being they struck with the edge of the sword until they had destroyed them; they did not leave any [one] that breathed.

R.14: The {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} kept for themselves all the valuable things and the animals from these towns. But they killed all the people with the sword until every one of them was destroyed. They did not leave anyone alive.

decisions.choice: the spoil and the livestock: taken by Israel, unlike at Jericho
decisions.reason: At Jericho everything was devoted to the LORD and nothing could be taken (6:17-19; 7:1). At Ai the LORD allowed Israel to keep the livestock and spoil (8:2, 27), as Moses' Israel had done with the towns of Sihon and Og (Deuteronomy 2:34-35; 3:6-7). The same rule applies here: the ban fell on the people, not on their goods.

decisions.choice: every human: people, as distinct from animals
decisions.reason: The word means human beings in general. It sets the people of the towns against the livestock just named.

decisions.choice: destroyed them: wiped them out
decisions.reason: This verb is not the verb "devote" but a general word for destroying completely (Deuteronomy 7:23-24). It is used again in verse 20.

decisions.choice: all the spoil ... the children of Israel plundered for themselves
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew order, which puts what was taken before the verb, setting it against "only every human".

records.source: כַּאֲשֶׁ֨ר צִוָּ֤ה יְהוָה֙ אֶת־מֹשֶׁ֣ה עַבְדּ֔וֹ כֵּן־צִוָּ֥ה מֹשֶׁ֖ה אֶת־יְהוֹשֻׁ֑עַ וְכֵן֙ עָשָׂ֣ה יְהוֹשֻׁ֔עַ לֹֽא־הֵסִ֣יר דָּבָ֔ר מִכֹּ֛ל אֲשֶׁר־צִוָּ֥ה יְהוָ֖ה אֶת־מֹשֶֽׁה׃
records.gloss: Just as commanded Yahweh Moses his servant, so commanded Moses Joshua, and so did Joshua; not he turned aside a word of all that had commanded Yahweh Moses.
pieces: Just as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} servant Moses, so Moses had commanded Joshua, and that is what Joshua did. He left nothing undone of all that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded Moses.

L.15: As {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded Moses {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} slave, so Moses commanded Joshua, and so Joshua did; he did not set aside a thing of all that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded Moses.

R.15: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} had given commands to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} servant Moses, and Moses had passed the same commands on to Joshua. Joshua obeyed them. He did everything {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded Moses, and he did not leave out anything.

decisions.choice: the LORD commanded Moses, Moses commanded Joshua, Joshua did: one line of command
decisions.reason: The verse links the three in a chain. Moses had handed on the LORD's charge to Joshua (Deuteronomy 31:7-8, 23), and the LORD had told Joshua to keep all that Moses commanded (1:7). Here Joshua is shown to have done so.

decisions.choice: he did not turn aside a word: he left nothing undone
decisions.reason: The verb means to remove or set aside, and the noun means both "word" and "thing". Joshua did not set aside any part of what he was commanded.

decisions.choice: slave (L); servant (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in verse 12 and 1:1.

records.source: וַיִּקַּ֨ח יְהוֹשֻׁ֜עַ אֶת־כָּל־הָאָ֣רֶץ הַזֹּ֗את הָהָ֤ר וְאֶת־כָּל־הַנֶּ֨גֶב֙ וְאֵת֙ כָּל־אֶ֣רֶץ הַגֹּ֔שֶׁן וְאֶת־הַשְּׁפֵלָ֖ה וְאֶת־הָעֲרָבָ֑ה וְאֶת־הַ֥ר יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל וּשְׁפֵלָתֹֽה׃
records.gloss: And took Joshua all the land this: the hill country and all the Negev and all [the] land of the Goshen and the Shephelah and the Arabah and [the] hill country of Israel and its Shephelah,
pieces: So Joshua took this whole land: the hill country, all the Negev, all the land of Goshen, the foothills, the Arabah, and the hill country of Israel with its foothills,

L.16: And Joshua took all this land: the hill country and all the Negev and all the land of Goshen and the Shephelah and the Arabah and the hill country of Israel and its Shephelah,

R.16: So Joshua took control of this whole land. He took the hills, all the southern desert, all the area of Goshen, the low hills in the west, and the Jordan Valley. He also took the hills of Israel and the low hills beside them.

decisions.choice: the hill country, the Negev, the Shephelah, the Arabah: the whole land, south and north
decisions.reason: The summary names the regions as in 10:40-41 and Deuteronomy 1:7: the central hills, the dry south (Negev), the low hills toward the coast (Shephelah) and the Jordan valley (Arabah). It joins the southern campaign of chapter 10 to the northern one of this chapter.

decisions.choice: the land of Goshen: a district in the south of Canaan
decisions.reason: This Goshen is in the hills of southern Judah (10:41; 15:51), not the land of Goshen in Egypt where Israel once lived (Genesis 45:10).

decisions.choice: the hill country of Israel: the hills north of Judah
decisions.reason: It is set beside "the hill country of Judah" in verse 21: the central hills that later belonged to the northern tribes. The names reflect how the land came to be divided.

decisions.choice: foothills (B); the southern desert, the low hills in the west, the Jordan Valley (R)
decisions.reason: As in verse 2 and Deuteronomy 1:7. Readable ends its sentences here and begins verse 17 with a new one.

records.source: מִן־הָהָ֤ר הֶֽחָלָק֙ הָעוֹלֶ֣ה שֵׂעִ֔יר וְעַד־בַּ֤עַל גָּד֙ בְּבִקְעַ֣ת הַלְּבָנ֔וֹן תַּ֖חַת הַר־חֶרְמ֑וֹן וְאֵ֤ת כָּל־מַלְכֵיהֶם֙ לָכַ֔ד וַיַּכֵּ֖ם וַיְמִיתֵֽם׃
records.gloss: from the mountain the Halak that goes up [to] Seir and as far as Baal-gad in [the] valley of the Lebanon under Mount Hermon; and all their kings he captured, and he struck them and put them to death.
pieces: from Mount Halak, rising toward Seir, to Baal-gad in the Lebanon valley below Mount Hermon. He captured all their kings, struck them down and put them to death.

L.17: from Mount Halak, that goes up [toward] Seir, and as far as Baal-gad in the valley of the Lebanon below Mount Hermon. And all their kings he captured, and he struck them and put them to death.

R.17: The land reached from Mount Halak in the south, on the way up to Seir, to Baal-gad in the north, in the Lebanon Valley at the foot of Mount Hermon. Joshua captured all the kings of this land and put them to death.

decisions.choice: Mount Halak, which goes up to Seir: the southern limit
decisions.reason: The name means "the bare" or "smooth" mountain. It lay in the far south, on the way toward Seir, the hill country of Edom, and marks the same southern limit in 12:7. Its exact site is not known.

decisions.choice: Baal-gad in the valley of Lebanon: the northern limit
decisions.reason: Baal-gad lay in the valley between the Lebanon range and Mount Hermon (12:7; 13:5). From Halak to Baal-gad is the whole land from south to north.

decisions.choice: struck them and put them to death: the kings were killed
decisions.reason: The two verbs together say that the captured kings were executed, as the kings of the south were in 10:26.

decisions.choice: in the south ... in the north
decisions.reason: Readable says which limit each place marks, so readers who do not know the names can follow the extent of the land (m1, m2).

decisions.choice: put them to death
decisions.reason: Readable gives the two verbs as one, since both say that the kings were killed.

records.source: יָמִ֣ים רַבִּ֗ים עָשָׂ֧ה יְהוֹשֻׁ֛עַ אֶת־כָּל־הַמְּלָכִ֥ים הָאֵ֖לֶּה מִלְחָמָֽה׃
records.gloss: Days many made Joshua with all the kings these war.
pieces: Joshua waged war against all these kings for a long time.

L.18: Many days Joshua made war with all these kings.

R.18: Joshua fought against all these kings for a long time.

decisions.choice: many days: a long time
decisions.reason: "Days" often means an indefinite stretch of time. The quick telling of chapters 10-11 is not meant to suggest a short war. Caleb's ages in 14:7 and 10, forty when the spies were sent and eighty-five when the land was divided, suggest that the wars lasted some years.

decisions.choice: many days first: the length of the war stressed
decisions.reason: The Hebrew puts "many days" at the head of the sentence, to stress how long the fighting went on.

records.source: לֹֽא־הָיְתָ֣ה עִ֗יר אֲשֶׁ֤ר הִשְׁלִ֨ימָה֙ אֶל־בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל בִּלְתִּ֥י הַחִוִּ֖י יֹשְׁבֵ֣י גִבְע֑וֹן אֶת־הַכֹּ֖ל לָקְח֥וּ בַמִּלְחָמָֽה׃
records.gloss: Not there was a city that made peace with [the] sons of Israel except the Hivite[s], [the] inhabitants of Gibeon; all [of them] they took in battle.
pieces: Not one town made peace with the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} except the Hivites who lived in Gibeon. All the others they took in battle.

L.19: There was not a city that made peace with the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel except the Hivites, the inhabitants of Gibeon; all [the rest] they took in battle.

R.19: None of the towns made a peace treaty with the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} except Gibeon, where the Hivites lived. Israel had to fight to take all the others.

decisions.choice: the Hivites, the inhabitants of Gibeon: the one people who came to terms
decisions.reason: Chapter 9 tells how the Gibeonites, who were Hivites (9:7), tricked Israel into a treaty and so were spared (9:15, 26-27).

decisions.choice: made peace: came to terms, surrendered under a treaty
decisions.reason: The verb means to make peace or to submit on terms, as in Deuteronomy 20:12 and 2 Samuel 10:19. No other town sought such terms.

decisions.choice: all: all the rest
decisions.reason: "All" means all the towns other than Gibeon, which the verse has just set apart.

decisions.choice: all [the rest] (L); all the others (B, R)
decisions.reason: The words make plain that "all" leaves out Gibeon (m3).

records.source: כִּ֣י מֵאֵ֣ת יְהוָ֣ה׀הָיְתָ֡ה לְחַזֵּ֣ק אֶת־לִבָּם֩ לִקְרַ֨את הַמִּלְחָמָ֤ה אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ לְמַ֣עַן הַֽחֲרִימָ֔ם לְבִלְתִּ֥י הֱיוֹת־לָהֶ֖ם תְּחִנָּ֑ה כִּ֚י לְמַ֣עַן הַשְׁמִידָ֔ם כַּאֲשֶׁ֛ר צִוָּ֥ה יְהוָ֖ה אֶת־מֹשֶֽׁה׃ס
records.gloss: For from Yahweh it was to strengthen their heart to meet the battle with Israel, in order to devote them to destruction, that not would be to them favor, but in order to destroy them, just as had commanded Yahweh Moses.
pieces: For it was {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} who made their hearts stubborn, so that they came out to meet Israel in battle, in order that they would be devoted to destruction and receive no mercy, but be wiped out, just as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded Moses.

L.20: For it was from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} to make their heart strong to meet Israel in battle, in order to devote them to destruction, so that there would be no favor for them, but in order to destroy them, as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded Moses.

R.20: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} had made these peoples stubborn, so that they went to war against Israel. He did this so that they would be destroyed completely, as people given over to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and be shown no mercy. They were to be wiped out, as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded Moses.

decisions.choice: the LORD made their hearts strong: God confirmed the peoples in their resolve to fight
alternatives: the LORD made them bold to fight
decisions.reason: The verb means to make firm or strong, and it is the one used when the LORD made Pharaoh's heart strong (Exodus 4:21; 14:4, 17) and Sihon's spirit hard (Deuteronomy 2:30). The heart in Hebrew is the seat of thought and will. The same verb is used in the command to Joshua, "be strong" (1:6-9): here God makes the enemy strong in the wrong way, firm in a choice that leads to their ruin. The kings had chosen to gather and fight (9:1-2; 10:1-5; 11:1-5), and in Exodus Pharaoh hardened his own heart as well as being hardened by God (Exodus 8:11, 28). As there, both are held together, and the text does not explain how. The verse gives the reason why no town but Gibeon made peace (verse 19): the war and its outcome were in the LORD's hands. It does not say that peace was closed to anyone who sought it; Rahab, who turned to the LORD (2:9-13; 6:25), and the Gibeonites (chapter 9) were spared.

decisions.choice: that they would be shown no favor: that no mercy would be granted them
alternatives: so that they would make no plea for mercy
decisions.reason: The noun belongs with the verb "show favor" and often means a plea for favor (1 Kings 8:28; Jeremiah 36:7). The phrase can therefore mean either that the peoples would receive no mercy, as Deuteronomy 7:2 commands ("show them no favor", the same root), or that they would make no plea for mercy, which would explain why none sought terms (verse 19). The link with Deuteronomy 7:2 and the closing words "as the LORD had commanded Moses" favor the first.

decisions.choice: devote to destruction ... destroy: the command of Deuteronomy
decisions.reason: The two purposes restate the command of Deuteronomy 7:2 and 20:16-17, the first with the verb "devote" (verses 11-12) and the second with the general verb "destroy" (verse 14). The note at Deuteronomy 7:2 sets out what that book says about the reasons and limits of the ban: it applied to the peoples of this land and was grounded in their worship and their wrongs (Deuteronomy 9:4-5; 20:18).

decisions.choice: in order to ... but in order to: God's purpose, not only the result
decisions.reason: The two clauses say what the hardening was for. The subject of "devote" and "destroy" is not named; the context shows it is Israel acting at the LORD's command.

decisions.choice: make their heart strong (L); made their hearts stubborn (B); made these peoples stubborn (R)
decisions.reason: As in Exodus 4:21, where the same verb is used: Literal keeps "make strong"; Balanced and Readable say "stubborn", since a heart made strong here is one set firmly against God's purpose. Literal keeps the singular "heart" of the Hebrew, which speaks of the peoples together.

decisions.choice: these peoples; He did this so that ...
decisions.reason: Readable names who "they" are, the peoples and kings of the land who fought (verse 19), and splits the long sentence, repeating the subject. It gives "devote to destruction" in plain words, as in verse 11.

records.source: וַיָּבֹ֨א יְהוֹשֻׁ֜עַ בָּעֵ֣ת הַהִ֗יא וַיַּכְרֵ֤ת אֶת־הָֽעֲנָקִים֙ מִן־הָהָ֤ר מִן־חֶבְרוֹן֙ מִן־דְּבִ֣ר מִן־עֲנָ֔ב וּמִכֹּל֙ הַ֣ר יְהוּדָ֔ה וּמִכֹּ֖ל הַ֣ר יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל עִם־עָרֵיהֶ֖ם הֶחֱרִימָ֥ם יְהוֹשֻֽׁעַ׃
records.gloss: And came Joshua at the time that and cut off the Anakim from the hill country, from Hebron, from Debir, from Anab, and from all [the] hill country of Judah and from all [the] hill country of Israel; with their cities devoted them to destruction Joshua.
pieces: At that time Joshua went and wiped out the Anakim from the hill country: from Hebron, Debir and Anab, and from the whole hill country of Judah and of Israel. He devoted them to destruction together with their towns.

L.21: And Joshua came at that time and cut off the Anakim from the hill country, from Hebron, from Debir, from Anab, and from all the hill country of Judah, and from all the hill country of Israel; with their cities Joshua devoted them to destruction.

R.21: At that time Joshua went and destroyed the Anakim who lived in the hill country. He removed them from Hebron, Debir and Anab, and from all the hills of Judah and of Israel. He destroyed them and their towns completely, as given over to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: the Anakim: a people known for their great size
decisions.reason: The Anakim lived around Hebron, and the spies' fear of them had kept Israel out of the land forty years before (Numbers 13:22, 28, 33; Deuteronomy 1:28; 9:2). The people Israel once feared most are now driven out.

decisions.choice: cut off: removed, wiped out
decisions.reason: The verb means to cut off, and with people as its object, to destroy them or remove them from a place (7:9; 23:4).

decisions.choice: at that time: a summary of the war, which later chapters fill out
decisions.reason: The verse sums up what Joshua's campaigns achieved. Later chapters tell how Caleb took Hebron from the sons of Anak and how Othniel took Debir (14:12-15; 15:13-17), and the account of the war that Joshua led includes them. Hebron and Debir were also taken in the southern campaign (10:36-39).

decisions.choice: destroyed them ... completely, as given over to the LORD
decisions.reason: As in verse 11, Readable gives the sense of "devote to destruction" in plain words.

decisions.choice: wiped out (B); destroyed ... removed (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of "cut off" (m2). Readable uses two verbs, since the list says where they were removed from.

records.heading: The Anakim wiped out

records.source: לֹֽא־נוֹתַ֣ר עֲנָקִ֔ים בְּאֶ֖רֶץ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל רַ֗ק בְּעַזָּ֛ה בְּגַ֥ת וּבְאַשְׁדּ֖וֹד נִשְׁאָֽרוּ׃
records.gloss: Not was left Anakim in [the] land of [the] sons of Israel; only in Gaza, in Gath, and in Ashdod they remained.
pieces: In the land of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} no Anakim were left; some remained only in Gaza, Gath and Ashdod.

L.22: There were no Anakim left in the land of the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel; only in Gaza, in Gath, and in Ashdod they remained.

R.22: There were no Anakim left anywhere in the land of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}. Some of them still lived only in the towns of Gaza, Gath and Ashdod.

decisions.choice: Gaza, Gath, Ashdod: towns of the southern coastal plain, later held by the Philistines
decisions.reason: These three are among the five Philistine cities named in 13:3. They lay outside the land Israel held at this time. Goliath, the giant of 1 Samuel 17:4, came from Gath.

decisions.choice: only ... they remained: a remnant left outside Israel's land
decisions.reason: The verse limits verse 21: the Anakim were gone from Israel's land, but some survived in these towns.

decisions.choice: some
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "they remained"; Balanced and Readable add "some" because only a remnant of the Anakim is meant.

records.source: וַיִּקַּ֨ח יְהוֹשֻׁ֜עַ אֶת־כָּל־הָאָ֗רֶץ כְּ֠כֹל אֲשֶׁ֨ר דִּבֶּ֣ר יְהוָה֮ אֶל־מֹשֶׁה֒ וַיִּתְּנָהּ֩ יְהוֹשֻׁ֨עַ לְנַחֲלָ֧ה לְיִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל כְּמַחְלְקֹתָ֖ם לְשִׁבְטֵיהֶ֑ם וְהָאָ֥רֶץ שָׁקְטָ֖ה מִמִּלְחָמָֽה׃פ
records.gloss: And took Joshua all the land according to all that had spoken Yahweh to Moses, and gave it Joshua as an inheritance to Israel according to their divisions by their tribes. And the land was quiet from war.
pieces: So Joshua took the entire land, just as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had told Moses, and he gave it to Israel as an inheritance, divided among their tribes. And the land had peace from war.

L.23: And Joshua took the whole land, according to all that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had spoken to Moses, and Joshua gave it as an inheritance to Israel according to their divisions by their tribes. And the land was quiet from war.

R.23: So Joshua took the whole land, just as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had promised Moses. He gave it to Israel to be their own lasting share, and he divided it among their tribes. Then the land had peace, and the fighting stopped.

decisions.choice: the whole land: the decisive conquest, with work still to be done
decisions.reason: The verse closes the account of the wars by saying that the LORD's word to Moses was fulfilled (Deuteronomy 31:3-8). Soon after, the LORD tells Joshua that "very much land" remains to be taken (13:1-6), and later chapters speak of peoples still living among the tribes (15:63; 16:10; 17:12-13; 23:4-5). "The whole land" describes the breaking of the power of the land's kings, not the end of every task.

decisions.choice: inheritance: a share of land held by a family for good
decisions.reason: The word names land received and handed down within a family and tribe (Numbers 26:52-56; 34:13). The division itself is told in chapters 13-21.

decisions.choice: according to their divisions by their tribes: the land divided by tribe and clan
decisions.reason: The first noun means a share or division; with "by their tribes" it means that each tribe received its portion (12:7; 18:10).

decisions.choice: the land was quiet from war: there was peace
decisions.reason: The verb means to be quiet or at rest. The same words close 14:15, and Judges uses them for the years of peace after each rescue (Judges 3:11, 30).

decisions.choice: the land had peace
decisions.reason: As the book-wide choice for this phrase: Literal "was quiet", Balanced and Readable "had peace".

decisions.choice: promised; their own lasting share
decisions.reason: Readable says "promised" for what the LORD had spoken, since his word to Moses about the land was a promise (Deuteronomy 31:3-8), and explains "inheritance" (m2).
